chapter_title: Early Humans and Beginning of Civilisation

questions.question_text: Which core concept is central to the discussion in Section 1 of Early Humans and Beginning of Civilisation?
Which was the first hominin species to migrate out of Africa?
According to Chapter 4, which factor plays a vital role in shaping societal or natural structures?
options: A) Scientific evidence and systematic processes
questions.correct_answer: A) Scientific evidence and systematic processes

questions.question_text: State two distinctive features of the Neolithic site of Mehrgarh.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) It provides the earliest evidence of barley and wheat cultivation and sheep/goat domestication in South Asia (~7000 BCE). 2) Inhabitants lived in rectangular mud-brick houses and created early earthenware pottery. Key points: Earliest South Asian farming evidence (~7000 BCE), Mud-brick settled architecture

questions.question_text: Why do historians divide early human history into different ages such as Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Historians categorize prehistoric eras based on the dominant material technology used for tools, weapons, and daily implements. This material progress reflects advancements in human knowledge, pyrotechnology, trade networks, and social organization.

questions.question_text: Explain how surplus food production in the Neolithic period led to the rise of Bronze Age civilisations.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Farming innovations provided stable food surpluses. 2) Surpluses freed a portion of the population from direct food production, enabling specialization in crafts (pottery, metallurgy), administration, and trade. 3) Craft specialization spurred metallurgical advancements (smelting copper and tin into bronze). 4) Urban trade networks required record-keeping, driving script invention. 5) Centralized governance emerged to manage irrigation and trade, creating Bronze Age cities.

questions.question_text: Source Passage (The period before writing is understood through archaeology....): Which ancient civilisation used the cuneiform script?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The Mesopotamian civilisation in the Tigris-Euphrates valley.

questions.question_text:
Read the scenario and answer the question:
'Archaeologists excavating a site discover stone grinding slabs, charred wheat grains, animal bones showing domestic butchery marks, and fired clay storage jars.'

Question: Which prehistoric era does this site belong to? Justify your choice.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Neolithic period. Justification: Grain cultivation (wheat), animal husbandry, grain processing tools (grinding slabs), and storage pottery are core hallmarks of Neolithic food production.

hotspots.label: Palaeolithic Era
hotspots.description: Old Stone Age: Crude core/flake tools, hand axes, hunter-gatherer bands (Bhimbetka)

hotspots.label: Mesolithic Era
hotspots.description: Middle Stone Age: Geometric microliths (<3cm), hafted spears, rock cave art

hotspots.label: Neolithic Era
hotspots.description: New Stone Age: Polished celts, Mehrgarh (~7000 BCE) farming revolution, village settlements
